assets.defect_engineered: Converts to several addressable text frames PLUS two real graphic frames (workable per-frame), but the body story's textContent readout silently omits the 19-character italic run 'the meadow you walk' while keeping its line break, so every character offset past it is short by exactly 19; the validator returns VALID with zero warnings and the prepare step reports completed, yet the GIFT_TOTAL and GIVING_LEVEL placeholders that sit AFTER the dropped run fall outside the recomputed frame text and silently fail to bind (checkpoint after step 7).
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's press file of last year's COMMUNITY letter (one page, photographed; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single page, US Letter 8.5 x 11 in PORTRAIT, 3 mm bleed present, fonts embedded, one placed preserve photograph and the trust mark placed as artwork. This is the WARM register mailed to most donors (Friend / Meadow / Steward).

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED:
- Top band: the heron-and-ring MARK placed top-left as artwork, RIVERMEADOW TRUST set beside it, the tagline 'Land held in common, kept for good' beneath.
- A placed PRESERVE PHOTOGRAPH across the upper third (the per-region image, one meadow per donor's county).
- A warm body letter: a salutation line, two grateful paragraphs that name the field, a GIFT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT sentence carrying the year total and the giving level, and the executive director's sign-off.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (conversion reality + the reverse-engineering trap):
- Because it carries placed images the page converts to SEVERAL addressable text frames PLUS TWO real graphic frames (one for the mark, one for the preserve photo). This is workable and a per-frame mapping strategy IS available here.
- The trap is in the READOUT, not the structure: the body story's textContent SILENTLY OMITS one styled run while keeping its line break. The dropped run is the italicised preserve phrase 'the meadow you walk' (EXACTLY 19 characters) set mid-paragraph just before the gift line. Every character offset computed past that point is therefore SHORT BY EXACTLY 19; the returned string still looks well-formed; the mapping validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets; and the placeholder/prepare step reports completed successfully.
- Consequence: the early placeholders (SALUTATION, opening) land, but the two placeholders that sit AFTER the dropped run — GIFT_TOTAL and GIVING_LEVEL — fall outside the recomputed frame text and silently fail to bind, leaving no trace in any tool response. Rebuilding offsets against the document's OWN reconstructed story text, then re-preparing and reading the placeholders back, is the only fix.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): SALUTATION | PRESERVE_PHOTO | GIFT_TOTAL | GIVING_LEVEL | ED_SIGNOFF

Colours: Cream Stock #F3EEE2 ground, River Slate #2E4A45 headings and rules, Field Ink #2A2622 body, Meadow Green #6E7F4E accents.

LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's press file of last year's LEADERSHIP letter (one page, cream stock, typographic, NO photograph; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single page, US Letter 8.5 x 11 in PORTRAIT, 3 mm bleed present, fonts embedded, NO placed images anywhere in the file. This is the QUIET register mailed to the leadership circle (Easement / Legacy / Guardian).

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent elements):
- A SALUTATION block, upper left, personal.
- A BODY of three restrained paragraphs, wide margins, no emphasis.
- A GIFT ACKNOWLEDGEMENT line stating the year total and the leadership level, set without weight.
- A SIGNATURE block: the executive director's sign-off, name and title, sitting like a real signature.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- Because there are NO images anywhere in the file, the whole page converts to EXACTLY ONE continuous text frame and ZERO graphic frames. The four apparent elements are four STYLED PARAGRAPHS inside a SINGLE story, not four addressable frames.
- Therefore the per-frame mapping strategy that works on the community sibling is NOT available here: SALUTATION, GIFT_TOTAL, GIVING_LEVEL and ED_SIGNOFF all have to be mapped BY POSITION inside one flow.
- And with ZERO graphic frames there is NOWHERE to bind the recovered mark as a placed graphic; the mark must be handled differently for this letter (anchored into the flow as a character object, or carried on the pre-printed stationery) rather than placed per record.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens, ALL inside one story): SALUTATION | GIFT_TOTAL | GIVING_LEVEL | ED_SIGNOFF

Colours: Cream Stock #F3EEE2 ground, Field Ink #2A2622 body, River Slate #2E4A45 rule and signature.

assets.defect_engineered: The NAME & ADDRESS block is a fixed-measure text frame (72 mm wide, two lines, no auto-size and no linked overflow), so an overset salutation does not spill, does not warn and does not error: it stops rendering at the frame edge and truncates the longest households ('Mr. and Mrs. Prescott Vandeleur', the double-barrelled couples) MID-WORD at trim while the page count stays exactly right and every tool reports success (checkpoint after step 13).

LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's press file of the statutory GIFT RECEIPT (one record shown; identical for every donor; to be reverse-engineered downstream).

Document: single page, US Letter 8.5 x 11 in PORTRAIT, fonts embedded. The registration line and the acknowledgement paragraph are STATUTORY and MUST NOT be altered.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED:
- Header: the trust wordmark and the line 'Rivermeadow Trust - Official Gift Receipt'.
- A NAME & ADDRESS block, upper left, carrying the household salutation and mailing address.
- A GIFT SUMMARY line: total contributions for the year and the receipt date.
- A fixed STATUTORY PARAGRAPH: 'Rivermeadow Trust is a 501(c)(3) organization, EIN 06-3319847. No goods or services were provided in exchange for this contribution. Please retain this receipt for your tax records.'

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the trap):
- The NAME & ADDRESS block is a FIXED-MEASURE text frame, 72 mm wide by two lines tall, with NO auto-size and NO linked overflow frame. An overset line does not spill into another frame, does not raise an overset warning, and does not error: it simply STOPS RENDERING at the right frame edge.
- At trim this TRUNCATES the longest household salutations MID-WORD while the page count stays exactly right and every tool in the chain reports success. Which records overflow depends on the salutations written into the data downstream: the longest households in the export ('Mr. and Mrs. Prescott Vandeleur', 'Dr. Rosalind Featherstonehaugh-Wetherby', 'Marguerite L'Estrange-Postlethwaite', 'The Halvorsen-Achterberg Household') run past 72 mm and are the ones that clip. The fix is a DATA decision (shorten/restructure those salutations) or moving the field to a frame that can carry it, then a re-merge.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): SALUTATION | ADDRESS | GIFT_TOTAL | RECEIPT_DATE

Colours: white ground, Field Ink #2A2622 body, River Slate #2E4A45 header rule.

assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, shot slightly from below at a small angle, of a rectangular CAST BRONZE donor plaque bolted to a weathered granite post at a woodland trailhead, lit by uneven late-afternoon daylight so the LEFT THIRD of the casting falls into soft shadow where the raised bronze and its green-brown patina run close together in VALUE with little contrast. Cast into the plaque in RAISED RELIEF is a compound circular emblem: a heron in flight over a curved river bend at the centre, enclosed by a RING of small-caps type reading RIVERMEADOW TRUST separated from a lower motto by a single THIN HAIRLINE RULE that is barely thicker than the letter strokes, the small-caps letters set tight with small closed counters. Real 20-year-old bronze with green patina in the recesses, faint scratches and water-staining, warm metal highlights on the raised edges, casual real-world snapshot look with slight handheld softness, not a studio shot. No modern brand names, no real trademarks.

RIVERMEADOW TRUST - APPROVED YEAR-END COPY (board approved; the receipt paragraph is fixed and must not be edited)

GIVING LEVELS AND THRESHOLDS (annual household total; use to resolve any blank level)
- Friend of the Valley: $25 to $99
- Meadow Circle: $100 to $499
- Steward's Circle: $500 to $1,499
- Easement Circle: $1,500 to $4,999
- Legacy Circle: $5,000 to $14,999
- Guardian of the Valley: $15,000 and above
(Friend, Meadow and Steward receive the COMMUNITY letter. Easement, Legacy and Guardian receive the LEADERSHIP letter.)

COMMUNITY LETTER (warm register - most donors)
[Salutation],

The hay came in twice off the lower fields this year, and the herons were back on the river by April. None of that happens on its own. It happens because neighbours like you decided the valley was worth keeping.

Your giving this year came to [Gift Total], which places you among our [Giving Level]. Whatever the size, it went straight into the land - into the meadow you walk, into the easements that keep the fields as fields.

Thank you for keeping the valley in common hands. We will see you on the trails.

With gratitude,
[ED Sign-off]

LEADERSHIP LETTER (quiet register - leadership circle)
[Salutation],

I wanted to write to you myself. The work we were able to do this year - forty more acres held under easement, the Fenn Hollow trail reopened, the river bend at Weir Brook kept open to the public - rested on the households who carry this trust. Yours is one of them.

Your support this year, [Gift Total], places you in our [Giving Level]. I do not take it for granted, and neither does the board.

The land will outlast all of us. That is the point of it, and it is why your generosity matters the way it does.

Yours,
[ED Sign-off]

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR SIGN-OFF
Claire Ashford
Executive Director, Rivermeadow Trust

STATUTORY GIFT RECEIPT WORDING (fixed - do not alter)
Rivermeadow Trust is a 501(c)(3) organization, EIN 06-3319847. No goods or services were provided in exchange for this contribution. Please retain this receipt for your tax records.
